permissions.loadError: The permission catalog could not be loaded.

roles.title: Roles
roles.description: Roles bundle permissions. Built-in roles are fixed; custom roles are defined per product.
roles.customDescription: Defined for this product. Editable by users with roles:manage.
roles.customEmptyBody: Create a role when the built-in roles do not fit.
roles.editorDescription: Choose the permissions this role grants. Changes apply immediately to everyone who holds the role.
roles.name: Name
roles.deleteBody: The role “{{name}}” is deleted permanently. A role that is still assigned to members or operators cannot be deleted: give them another role first.
roles.keyHelp: Stable identifier used in memberships, e.g. “support_agent”. Cannot be changed later.

scopeHelp.product: Assigned to product operators; may hold product and tenant permissions.
scopeHelp.tenant: Assigned to tenant members; holds tenant permissions only.

roles.keyInfo: 2–41 lowercase letters, digits or underscores. Built-in keys such as “member” cannot be used.
roles.scopeInfo: The scope cannot be changed after the role is created.
roles.permissionsInfo: Platform permissions cannot be part of a role. Only people who hold all of a role's permissions can assign it to others (role ceiling).
roles.retiredKept: Retired permissions it keeps: {{permissions}}. They grant nothing while retired and are kept on save.

keys.title: API keys
keys.description: Keys let machines call the Axentra API for this product with an explicit permission list.
keys.createDescription: The secret is shown exactly once after creation.
keys.name: Name
keys.nameHelp: Describe where the key is used, e.g. “billing-worker production”.
keys.tenantScopeHelp: Optional. A tenant-scoped key can only access data of that tenant.
keys.emptyBody: Create a key for each service that calls the API.
keys.rotateBody: A replacement key with a new secret is created for “{{name}}”, with the same permissions, tenant scope and expiry. The old secret stops working when the grace period ends; update all services that use it. Keys created with the old key are not revoked.
keys.revokeBody: “{{name}}” stops working immediately, and so does every key that was created with it (and the keys created with those). This cannot be undone.
keys.secretWarningBody: It is shown only this once and cannot be recovered. Store it in a secret manager.
keys.secretConfirm: I have stored the secret securely
keys.expiryHelp: After this time the key stops working. Rotating the key keeps its expiry.
keys.expiryInfo: An expired key is refused and listed as Expired; its expiry cannot be extended, so create a new key in time. Keys that a service creates with another key never outlive that key (without their own expiry they inherit it); keys created here belong to your account, so that rule does not apply.
keys.expiryDateHelp: The key works until the end of this day in your time zone.
keys.grace: Grace period for the old secret
keys.graceHelp: Lets running services switch over without downtime.
keys.tenantScopeInfo: A tenant-bound key works only inside that tenant; its product permissions have no effect. It is refused while the tenant is suspended and deleted with the tenant.
keys.permissionsInfo: You can grant only permissions you hold yourself. Platform permissions are never available to API keys.
keys.graceInfo: During the grace period the old and the new key both work and both are listed as Active. Revoke the old key to end the grace period early.
keys.statusInfo: Active: works. Expired: past its expiry date. Revoked: revoked, or replaced by rotation after its grace period.
keys.lastUsedInfo: Time of the last successful request with this key. Updated at most once a minute.
keys.secretUsage: Send the secret with every request in the header “Authorization: Bearer <secret>” or “X-API-Key: <secret>”.
keys.creatorHint: A key works only as long as the person who created it still holds the permissions it uses.

catalog.title: Permissions
catalog.description: Everything that can be granted in this product: the permissions the product declares itself and Axentra’s built-in permissions. Products declare their permissions in their code or through the API; with permissions:manage you can declare them here too.
catalog.ownDescription: Declared by this product. Owners and admins hold them automatically; viewers and support hold the read-only ones.
catalog.ownEmpty: This product declares no permissions of its own
catalog.ownEmptyBody: Product code registers them (for example “crm.deals:approve”); custom roles and API keys can then grant them.
catalog.builtInDescription: Provided by Axentra for every product.
catalog.name: Permission
catalog.defaultRolesInfo: Product owners and admins always hold every active product permission, tenant owners and admins every tenant-scoped one. This column lists the other built-in roles that hold it.
catalog.declaredByInfo: Product code: registered by the product's code at start; change it there. API: declared over the HTTP API by someone with permissions:manage.

declare.title: Declare permission
declare.description: A permission declared here can be granted through custom roles and API keys. Your product code checks it.
declare.nameHelp: <namespace>.<resource>:<action>, lowercase, for example crm.deals:approve. Cannot be changed later.
declare.nameInvalid: Use <namespace>.<resource>:<action> in lowercase letters, digits and underscores, for example crm.deals:approve.

scopeHelp.tenant: Granted per tenant (tenant roles, tenant-scoped keys).
scopeHelp.product: Granted for the whole product (product roles, product-level keys).

declare.defaultRolesHelp: Owners and admins always hold it. Select further built-in roles that should hold it.
declare.readLikeHelp: Read-only roles (support and viewers) hold permissions that only read data.
declare.retireBody: {{name}} stops granting anything, also where custom roles and API keys still list it. Declaring it again restores it. Type the name to confirm.
